In this paper, we propose the Scribendi Score, which is a reference-less metric to evaluate GEC system outputs that strongly correlates with human judgement. We use the output of the 12 systems evaluated in CoNLL-2014's shared tasks for GEC. The test set consists of 1312 sentences.
Evaluating the performance of a machine translation, text summarization, text simplification or GEC system poses significant difficulties because there is more than one possible correct output.

We use GPT-2 without further fine tuning to measure the perplexity of a source and predictions from different models. If the perplexity score improves (i.e., decreases), then we check whether the predicted sentences are syntactically related to the source sentence.

Following the CoNLL-2014 shared task on grammatical error correction, for which all the results are publicly available, including the references and 12 system outputs, and simultaneously performed a human evaluation of the system outputs.
guideline: Human raters ranked the system outputs to produce a quality ranking.
